caption:
Your resume gets you into the room. It stops working the moment you're in it.

The 2026 hiring reports — Taggd, ManpowerGroup, the executive-search desks — say the same thing in different words: at senior level the filter shifted from credential to fitment. Bearing. How you hold a room. How you answer the hard question when it lands sideways.

And the market is paying for it. The same cycle cutting managers is handing CXOs 18–25% year-on-year increases, the fastest in a decade.

So when you're qualified and still overlooked, the honest answer is rarely competence. It's that the judgement call was made on presence, and nobody told you that was the test.

Presence is not personality. It's trained. Thirty-five years of command taught me that bearing, controlled tone and calculated silence are skills — drilled, corrected, repeated. They work in a boardroom for the same reason they work anywhere else.

topic.title: Senior hiring now rewards fitment, not resumes
topic.angle: This audience privately asks 'I'm qualified, so why am I overlooked?' and the data gives the honest answer: at senior level the filter stopped being the credential and became a judgement call made on bearing, how you hold a room, and how you answer the hard question.
topic.why_now: This is cycle-timely rather than breaking — the Taggd, ManpowerGroup and executive-search reports are 2026 publications, months old — but it is live this week as the direct counterweight to the layoff story: the same market cutting managers is paying CXOs 18–25% YoY increases, the fastest in a decade.
